key_insight: Rare ReLU gate disagreements, not the average gradient, determine whether finite-batch SGD can recover after pretraining, so population gradient flow can be qualitatively wrong.
engineering_relevance: For staged training or fine-tuning, this means recovery may fail unless batch size and update budget are large enough to sample the small set of disagreeing inputs.
method: Two-unit ReLU regression with a source task that aligns neurons and a target task that separates them.
Compare population gradient flow with online SGD under batch size b and step size η after source pretraining time T.
Track the rare wedge of inputs where gates disagree and bound its cumulative sampling probability along the exact recursion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, for T above about log(b/η), SGD can fail with high probability over a horizon of order e^{c/η}, while recovery from a gradient-flow checkpoint needs Nb ≳ e^{λT} and b ≳ ηe^{λT}; simulations show behavior collapses mainly as a function of bδ/η.
watch_item: The result is derived for a specific two-unit ReLU setup, so the threshold laws may not transfer directly to deeper or more realistic architectures without re-checking gate-disagreement dynamics.
paper_title: Rare Gate Disagreements Can Limit Plasticity: When Gradient Flow Mispredicts Finite-Batch SGD
